cards.name: Cartoon
cards.summary: Turns live action into a flat cel-shaded cartoon: smooths detail into a few flat shading bands and draws dark ink outlines along strong edges.
use_for: comic-panel style recap of a political event in a satire reel
stylised flashback or 'imagine this' segment in an explainer
illustrated look behind a title or quote card
transition into an animated/graphic section
avoid: faces turn waxy and lose identity at high Detail Radius
busy crowd shots become noisy outline soup
heavy render on 4K, slow previews on long clips

params.name: Render
params.does: what is drawn: 1 Fill only, 2 Edges only, 3 Fill & Edges

params.name: Detail Radius
params.does: blur radius used to simplify detail before shading

params.name: Detail Threshold
params.does: tolerance of the edge-preserving pre-blur; higher = more fine detail smoothed away (more abstract)

params.name: Shading Steps
params.does: number of flat tone bands in the fill

params.name: Shading Smoothness
params.does: softness of the transitions between bands (low = hard cel bands)

params.name: Threshold
params.does: edge-detection threshold that decides how many outlines are drawn (direction unverified: test 1.3-3 and compare)

params.name: Width
params.does: outline thickness in pixels

params.name: Opacity
params.does: outline opacity (%)

cards.scripting: Group headers (Fill, Edge, Advanced) are not addressable; set leaf names directly (Shading Steps, Width, Edge Contrast...). Render is a 3-item popup (1-based). Premiere has no direct equivalent (approximate with Posterize + Find Edges blended). Render 2 (Edges) gives a line-art look usable as a matte for a sketch reveal. The direction of the Edge Threshold control (more vs fewer outlines as it rises) is unverified.

verified.note: Flat posterised cel-shaded fill with dark speckled outlines on the foreground blocks, a small round motif and the stripes; reads clearly as a cartoon/comic panel.

cards.name: Color Emboss
cards.summary: Embosses the image like a raised relief while keeping its original colours, so edges get light/dark bevelled ridges.
use_for: stamped/relief texture on a logo or title layer
gritty hyper-detailed look on a still photo in a trailer
subtle edge punch blended with the original
avoid: high Contrast blows out into harsh grey halos
looks dated on faces; keep it to graphics or blend it back

params.name: Direction
params.does: angle of the virtual light source (degrees)

params.name: Relief
params.does: height of the emboss / offset in pixels

params.name: Contrast
params.does: strength of the relief shading (%)

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: mix the untouched image back in (%)

cards.scripting: Direction is an angle property (degrees, no clamp). Contrast range is 0-32767 but anything above ~500 is just harsh. Blend With Original is 0-100 (%).

verified.note: Original colours kept with bevelled light/dark ridges and a sharpened relief along every edge.

cards.name: Emboss
cards.summary: Converts the image to a grey bas-relief: flat grey everywhere except light and dark ridges along edges, like a stamped metal plate.
use_for: stamped coin/medal look on a logo or emblem
grey relief texture layer set to Overlay for grit on titles
stylised freeze-frame in a trailer
avoid: kills all colour; on footage it reads as a cheap filter
fine noise in the source becomes visible grain

params.name: Direction
params.does: angle of the virtual light source (degrees)

params.name: Relief
params.does: height of the emboss in pixels

params.name: Contrast
params.does: strength of the relief (%)

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: mix the original back in (%)

cards.equivalent: Color Emboss (closest; Premiere 2026 has no grey Emboss, add Black & White after it)
cards.scripting: Same property set as Color Emboss. For a textured overlay, duplicate the layer, apply Emboss, set the duplicate's blend mode to Overlay/Soft Light.

verified.note: Frame turns into a flat grey bas-relief with light/dark ridges on edges (only faint red/cyan fringes on the stripes).

cards.name: Find Edges
cards.summary: Replaces the image with its detected edges: coloured lines on white (or glowing lines on black when inverted), like a sketch or X-ray outline.
use_for: sketch-to-photo reveal in a documentary intro
neon outline look (Invert on) for a tech/AI explainer
outline matte for a stylised transition
comic/drawn look combined with Posterize
avoid: noisy or compressed footage turns into speckle
full strength is unreadable on wide crowd shots

params.name: Invert
params.does: 0 = dark edges on white, 1 = bright edges on black

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: mixes the original image back in

cards.scripting: Invert is a checkbox (0/1). Blend With Original was harvested with range 0-1 even though the UI shows a percent; the exact scaling is unverified, keep values in 0-1. For a sketch reveal, keyframe Blend With Original from 0 to the top of the range, or crossfade an un-effected duplicate.

verified.note: Inverted mode gives thin glowing coloured edge lines on black, like a neon/x-ray outline of the scene.

cards.name: Glow
cards.summary: Finds the bright parts of the image (or alpha edges) and blooms them outward into a soft light halo, for neon, highlight bloom and dreamy looks.
use_for: neon glow on titles, lower thirds and line graphics
soft highlight bloom on a cinematic trailer shot
glowing map lines / route animations in an explainer
flash bloom at a hard cut or impact
avoid: low threshold (under ~50%, raw 128) on bright daylight footage blows the whole frame to white with false-colour blobs
stacking several Glows with big radius kills render speed
on flat news footage it can look cheap; keep it subtle

params.name: Glow Based On
params.does: 1 Alpha Channel (glows around the layer shape), 2 Color Channels (glows bright pixels)

params.name: Glow Threshold
params.does: brightness above which pixels glow; raw 0-255 (153 = 60%)

params.name: Glow Radius
params.does: size of the halo in pixels

params.name: Glow Intensity
params.does: brightness multiplier of the halo

params.name: Composite Original
params.does: 1 On Top, 2 Behind, 3 None (glow only)

params.name: Glow Operation
params.does: blend mode of the glow (popup, 25 items)

params.name: Glow Colors
params.does: 1 Original Colors, 2 A & B Colors, 3 Arbitrary Map

params.name: Color A
params.does: glow colour A when Glow Colors = A & B

cards.equivalent: Wonder Glow (Film Impact highlight bloom in Premiere 2026; Alpha Glow for alpha-edge glow only)
cards.scripting: Glow Threshold is the raw 0-255 value, not a percent (UI 60% = 153). Glow Intensity raw range goes to 255 but anything above ~5 is blown out. Glow Operation is a 25-item blend-mode popup (1 None, 2 Normal, 3 Add (default), 4 Multiply, 5 Dissolve, 6 Screen ... 25 Alpha Add; enum_labels (read from After Effects 26.0)); only 3 has been rendered. Color A/B only matter when Glow Colors = 2. For a classic layered glow, stack 2-3 Glows with increasing radius and decreasing intensity.

verified.note: Threshold 180 now blooms only the bright wall, white stripes and highlights into a warm soft halation while faces, stripes and foreground blocks stay readable, instead of v1's frame blown to white with magenta/blue false-colour blobs (the bright wall still glows close to white and leaves faint yellow/magenta fringes).

cards.name: Mosaic
cards.summary: Pixelates the layer into a grid of solid-colour blocks.
use_for: blur out a face, number plate or private document (with a mask or on a tracked solid)
pixel-dissolve transition between shots
retro 8-bit look for a gaming/internet-culture reel
censoring abusive text in a social post screenshot
avoid: too many (small) blocks leave faces and plates recognisable: for redaction keep blocks large (roughly 6-10 across a face) and track the mask; never rely on it alone for sensitive text
full-frame use reads as a glitch, not a style, if left too long

params.name: Horizontal Blocks
params.does: number of blocks across the layer

params.name: Vertical Blocks
params.does: number of blocks down the layer

params.name: Sharp Colors
params.does: 0 = averaged block colour, 1 = sampled colour (crisper)

cards.scripting: Blocks are counted over the layer's own size, so on a 1920x1080 layer use H:V = 16:9 for square pixels (e.g. 48x27). For censoring only part of the frame, put Mosaic on an adjustment layer with a mask, or on a duplicate layer with a mask. Sharp Colors is a checkbox (0/1). In Premiere the same effect is listed as "Mosaic (Legacy)"; Premiere's plain "Mosaic" is a different Film Impact effect.

verified.note: Whole frame pixelated into a 48x27 grid of solid-colour blocks.

cards.name: Motion Tile
cards.summary: Repeats the layer as tiles beyond its own edges, optionally mirrored, so you can move, shake or zoom the image without exposing empty edges.
use_for: edge fill for whip-pan / slide / shake transitions (Output Width/Height 300 + Mirror Edges)
camera shake or rotation without black corners
tiled grid of the same shot for a 'multiple screens' look
endless scrolling background pattern for an explainer
avoid: without Mirror Edges the seam between tiles is visible during moves
output size increases render cost; don't use more than needed

params.name: Tile Center
params.does: centre of the main tile (px); animate for a slide/offset

params.name: Tile Width
params.does: width of each tile as % of the layer
params.typical: 100 for edge fill, 33-50 for a grid

params.name: Tile Height
params.does: height of each tile as % of the layer
params.typical: 100 for edge fill, 33-50 for a grid

params.name: Output Width
params.does: width of the output area as % of the layer

params.name: Output Height
params.does: height of the output area as % of the layer

params.name: Mirror Edges
params.does: flips neighbouring tiles so seams are invisible

params.name: Phase
params.does: offsets alternate rows/columns (degrees)

cards.equivalent: Replicate (grid only; Premiere has no edge-extending Motion Tile, Offset gives a wrap-around shift)
cards.scripting: Output Width/Height above 100 extends beyond the layer bounds; the layer itself must be scaled/moved (Transform effect placed AFTER Motion Tile, or layer transform) to show the extra area. Classic whip-pan: Motion Tile (Output 300/300, Mirror Edges 1) then Transform effect keyframing Position by +/-1920 with Directional Blur. Mirror Edges and Horizontal Phase Shift are checkboxes (0/1); Phase is an angle.

verified.note: Image shrunk to 50% tiles and repeated in a 2x2 grid with mirrored edges.

cards.name: Posterize
cards.summary: Reduces each colour channel to a few tonal levels, producing flat colour bands like a screen print or poster.
use_for: poster / pop-art treatment of a leader photo for a satire reel
retro propaganda-poster look on a quote card background
graphic flashback or stylised freeze-frame
pairs with Cartoon/Find Edges for a comic look
avoid: skin tones break into ugly blotches at very low levels
gradients (sky) band badly; add slight blur or noise first

params.name: Level
params.does: number of tonal levels per channel

cards.scripting: Single integer property; keep 2-255. A slight Gaussian Blur before Posterize gives cleaner, larger shapes.

verified.note: Colours collapse into a few flat bands, screen-print/pop-art look.

cards.name: Roughen Edges
cards.summary: Distorts the layer's alpha edges with fractal noise so they look torn, eroded, rusty or photocopied; on a full-frame clip it roughens the frame border.
use_for: torn-paper cut-out for photos and newspaper clippings in a documentary
grungy edges on titles and stamps
eroding/boiling text reveal for a trailer title
scrapbook collage look in an explainer
avoid: works on alpha edges only: a full-frame shot only changes at the frame border
high Border on small text eats the letters

params.name: Edge Type
params.does: style of roughening (8-item popup)
params.typical: 1 Roughen, 3 Cut for torn paper, 5 Rusty for grunge

params.name: Border
params.does: depth of the roughened edge in pixels

params.name: Edge Sharpness
params.does: crisp vs soft edge

params.name: Fractal Influence
params.does: amount of fractal distortion (0-1)

params.name: Scale
params.does: size of the noise pattern (%)

params.name: Complexity
params.does: detail levels of the noise

params.name: Evolution
params.does: animates the noise shape (degrees)

params.name: Edge Color
params.does: colour of the edge band for the 'Color' edge types

cards.scripting: Operates on the layer's alpha: apply to text, shapes, keyed or masked layers, or a scaled-down photo; on a full-frame opaque clip only the frame border changes. Edge Type labels are read from After Effects 26.0. Evolution is an angle; Cycle Evolution is a checkbox (0/1). Offset (Turbulence) is in pixels. Edge Color only shows with the 'Color' edge types (2, 6, 8).

verified.note: Frame border is eaten into a torn, jagged black edge while the interior is untouched.

cards.name: Scatter
cards.summary: Randomly displaces pixels within a radius, dissolving the image into a frosted, diffused or sand-like scatter.
use_for: dissolve-into-dust transition on a title or photo
frosted-glass background behind text
disintegration effect on an old photo in a documentary
avoid: large amounts on faces look like a broken codec
static scatter on footage looks like a render error; animate it or keep it brief

params.name: Scatter Amount
params.does: radius of the pixel displacement

params.name: Grain
params.does: direction: 1 Both, 2 Horizontal, 3 Vertical

params.name: Scatter Randomness
params.does: re-randomise every frame (0/1); 1 makes it shimmer

cards.scripting: Scatter Randomness is a checkbox (Randomize Every Frame). Grain: 1 Both (default), 2 Horizontal, 3 Vertical (read from After Effects 26.0). Premiere has no Scatter; approximate with Noise + Gaussian Blur or a Turbulent Displace.

verified.note: Amount 150 dissolves the whole frame into a clearly visible frosted-glass scatter of displaced grains (faces and stripes reduced to soft granular shapes), where v1's Amount 60 was only a slight grainy softening.

cards.name: Strobe Light
cards.summary: Flashes the layer to a solid colour (or makes it transparent) on a fixed clock: each Period starts in the strobe colour, which holds for Period minus Duration, then the picture shows for the last Duration (Duration 0.1 / Period 0.5 = a 0.4 s flash twice a second). The clock is the layer's own, from its source's first frame. Measured under aerender frame for frame the same as Premiere's Strobe Light (same plug-in); Random Strobe Probablity between 0 and 100 turns it into random bursts.
use_for: paparazzi/press-conference camera flashes
lightning or power-flicker in a trailer
beat-synced flash on a music reel
random flicker for an old-film or horror vibe
avoid: Duration as the flash length: it is the gap, so a small Duration gives a long flash; for a one-frame flash at 25 fps set Duration = Period - 0.04

Trimmed layers: the clock runs from the source's first frame (the layer's startTime), not the in point, so a layer trimmed into its source can open mid-flash (trimmed to source 0.8 s, it was coloured on its first 3 frames)
A long regular strobe reads as mechanical: switch it off with a Blend With Original key or keep the burst short

Photosensitivity (Harding test / ITU-R BT.1702): no more than 3 flashes in any one second, and a flash to or from saturated red counts even when it is not bright. With Random Strobe Probablity 0 or 100 it flashes exactly once per Period (keep Period at 0.34 s or longer); any value in between inverts about that share of frames in random bursts (10 reached 7 flashes in one second, 50 also 7), which cannot be held under the limit. pve.check_scenes flags it.

params.name: Strobe Color
params.does: colour of the flash

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: how much original shows through the flash (%)

params.name: Strobe Duration (secs)
params.does: Despite the name, the un-coloured gap at the END of each Period: the colour holds for Period minus Duration, then the picture shows for Duration (0.1 of a 0.5 s Period = a 0.4 s flash; Duration equal to Period draws nothing). Measured identically in After Effects and Premiere
params.typical: Period minus the flash length (0.46 with a 0.5 Period = a one-frame flash at 25 fps)

params.name: Strobe Period (secs)
params.does: Time from the start of one flash to the next, in layer time from the source's first frame (a layer starting at comp 0.6 s flashes at comp 0.6, 1.1, 1.6 ...)

params.name: Random Strobe Probablity
params.does: Share (%) of frames inverted against the Probability-0 pattern, in bursts; the same seed gives the same pattern every render. 10 inverted 11% of frames, 50 about half; 100 is the exact inverse (colour only for the last Duration of each Period, so again one flash per Period)
params.typical: 0 (or 100); anything in between is a random burst generator

params.name: Strobe
params.does: 1 Operates On Color Only, 2 Makes Layer Transparent

params.name: Strobe Operator
params.does: how the strobe colour combines with the image (13-item popup)

pairs_with: Photosensitive flash rule (Harding / ITU-R BT.1702) and pve check
cards.scripting: Property name is misspelled in AE: use "Random Strobe Probablity" exactly. Measured 2026-10-13 under aerender (work/pve_live/strobe.json, per-frame luma at 25 fps): Duration 0.1 / Period 0.5 / Probability 0 gave 10 coloured frames then 2-3 picture frames every Period, on footage and on a grey solid, frame for frame the same as Premiere. Clock: layer time from startTime, i.e. the source's first frame: a layer starting at comp 0.6 s flashed at comp 0.6, 1.1, 1.6 ...; a layer trimmed to source 0.8 s flashed at source 1.0, 1.5 ... with its first 3 frames still coloured from the period that began at source 0.5. Probability 10 / 50 / 100 inverted 11% / 51% / 100% of the frames, the same frames on footage and on grey. The earlier 'no flash' gallery result was the harness: a 0.4 s comp on a layer starting at source 1.5 s, where Probability 100 colours only source 1.9-2.0 s, after the comp ended. Strobe: 1 Operates On Color Only, 2 Makes Layer Transparent; Strobe Operator: 1 Copy, 2 Add, 3 Subtract, 4 Multiply, 5 Difference, 6 And, 7 Or, 8 Xor, 9 Lighter, 10 Darker, 11 Minimum, 12 Maximum, 13 Screen (read from After Effects 26.0); only 1 has been rendered.

verified.note: Measured, not by eye: with the demo values the aerender strip is 10 coloured frames then 2-3 picture frames per 0.5 s Period (6 flashes in 2.8 s, at most 2 in one second), and the layer-at-0.6 s and trimmed-source renders follow the layer-time clock the card describes.

previous.why: the strobe measurement renders showed the effect works under aerender; the gallery's 'no flash' was its 0.4 s comp on a layer starting at source 1.5 s (with Probability 100 the colour fell after the comp ended)

verified.recheck: 2026-10-14: gallery frame pve/gallery/ae/200.png re-rendered in live wave 2 with the demo values: all 10 frames of its 0.4 s window (source 1.5-1.9 s) are white, the colour phase of the Period that starts at source 1.5 s, as the card's clock predicts; a still from this window cannot show a flash, so the measured strip stays the evidence

flash.basis: aerender measurements (work/pve_live/strobe.json): Probability 0 or 100 = one flash per Period (0.5 s Period: at most 2 in any second); 10 reached 7 in one second and 50 also 7 (random bursts). Blend With Original 90+ is PVE's faint-flash cut-off, not a measurement

cards.name: Texturize
cards.summary: Embosses the luminance of another layer (canvas, paper, brick, concrete) into this layer, so the image looks printed or painted on that texture.
use_for: photo or poster that looks pasted on a brick/concrete wall
canvas or paper texture on a title card or quote card
printed-newspaper feel on a headline screenshot
avoid: low-resolution textures look blurry and tiled
strong Texture Contrast on faces looks like skin disease

params.name: Texture Layer
params.does: layer whose luminance is used as the texture (layer reference)
params.typical: a hidden texture image in the same comp

params.name: Light Direction
params.does: angle of the light across the texture (degrees)

params.name: Texture Contrast
params.does: strength of the texture relief (0-2)

params.name: Texture Placement
params.does: 1 Tile Texture, 2 Center Texture, 3 Stretch Texture to Fit
params.typical: 1 for small textures, 3 for full-frame textures

cards.scripting: Needs a second layer: Texture Layer is a layer reference (set by layer index; 0 = none, the effect then does nothing). The texture layer can be hidden (video switch off) but must stay in the comp. AE reads the referenced layer's SOURCE, ignoring its effects and masks: a Fractal Noise solid only works as a texture after it is precomposed. Premiere 2026 has no Texture effect. Light Direction is an angle; Texture Placement is a 3-item popup.

verified.note: Card is needs_input (needs a Texture Layer reference), so the gallery did not render it.
